column1: # Manifest for the committed real-world parse-regression corpus in ./fixtures/.
# The fixtures themselves are checked in (see ./fixtures/) and parsed by
# check.sh, which fails if a file produces more ERROR nodes than its budget.
# Each fixture has a sibling <filename>.LICENSE recording its upstream project
# and license; the files remain under those licenses (see ./README.md).
# All listed scripts currently parse with zero ERROR nodes (budget 0). The
# column exists so a script exercising a documented limitation can be tracked
# with a non-zero budget rather than removed. Add new cases by dropping the
# file in ./fixtures/, adding a .LICENSE sibling, and a row here.
# Added from the broader stress-test sweep (see commit history).
# npocmaka/batch.scripts (MIT) — a torture-test collection of cmd idioms;
# included to guard the trickier edge cases (carets, (echo(), @@, delayed exp).
# Original Minimal Reproducible Examples (authored here, MIT) that distill
# idioms from scripts whose licenses prevent vendoring them verbatim.
